The fluid in the excavated portion of the north stormwater channel had an EC of 2.02 mS/cm.The east side of the well pad was being back-filled with gravel during this inspection. The berm of the secondary containment for the frac tank on the east side of the well pad is damaged.On Pad A, six wells are staged for production. Six GPUs are present within secondary containment. properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STL RESOURCES LLC

Violation Date: 2/29/2024
Violation Code: 78a66(b)1ii - REPORTING AND REMEDIATING SPILLS AND RELEASES – Reporting releases – Operator or other responsible party failed to report a spill or release of 5 gallons or more of a regulated substance over a 24-hour period that was not completely contained by secondary containment.
Violation ID: 8177871
Permit API: 035-21329
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton

Inspection Date: 2/29/2024
Comments: On February 29, 2024, DEP representative Brad Kline, Erica Lutz, and Evan Buck conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. The site was mostly stable except for the infiltration berm off the southwest corner of the well pad. This infiltration berm has a section of the berm eroded. The DEP recommend repairing the infiltration berm as soon as possible to prevent accelerated erosion of the area. The infiltration berms that were rebuilt as part of the cleanup effort from January 8, 2023 spill and the soil stockpile area do not meet the 70% vegetation requirement. There are a total of 5 wells capable of producing located on this well pad. Each well has a separator in line with it. All wells are tagged with API/well permit numbers. The well cellars are filled in with gravel. There are 5 GPUs and 4 steel vertical production fluids tanks onsite. Both the GPUs and production fluid tanks are stationed in secondary containment. The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad on January 8, 2022. The conductivity of the accumulated water in the northwest stormwater vault was 851 uS/cm. The conductivity of the accumulated water in the southwest stormwater vault was 651 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 20.5 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 20.9 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 21.6 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 15.4 uS/cm. Stream 1 control site had a conductivity of 20 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 95.2 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 78.7 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 36.5 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 29.6 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 48.2 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 22 uS/cm. No violations noted.

Violation ID: 8159674

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/21/2023
Comments: On September 21, 2023, inspection conducted at the Rumpelstiltskin well pad in Somerset Township, Washington County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3582382 where violations were issued in response to a spill caused by a GPU dumpline failure.The following was observed:At the time of inspection, the Act 9 sign was installed at the entrance of the access road and was not obstructed from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (see photo 1). The ERP was onsite (see photos 2 and 3). Some erosion rills were observed in the access road (see photos 4 and 5). Secondary containment was added to the GPU units onsite, and the impacted area was backfilled (see photos 10 and 11). A well tag was present on well 6H, with no observed leaks or discharge on the ground around it, and it appeared to be equipped for production (see photo 13). There are three other well heads onsite that also appear to be equipped for production (see photo 8). Production tanks were placed in secondary containment with no observed leaks with the containment (see photo 12). Seven rolloff dumpsters labeled "production water impacted solids" were onsite (see photos 7 and 9). After inspection was conducted, the Department spoke via phone with EQT representative David Crayne, who stated that remediation was complete and Act 2 is nearly ready for submittal to ECB. Based on observations from this inspection, the Department recommends that maintenance be conducted on the access road to prevent worsening accelerated erosion and sedimentation onsite. Closure of violations shall be contingent upon Act 2 approval and a subsequent CEI inspection.

Comments: On 3/9/23 a routine complete inspection of the McCoy 2 OG Well site was conducted. I was accompanied by Chase Ambrose (PA DEP).During the inspection the following was observed:-A well tag was observed on the wellhead (Photo #1).-The well and operator's information were displayed and visible at the well site as required by OGA 3211(g) (Photo #2). -Some corrosion was observed on the well and production equipment (Photos #3-4). -Two production tanks were present at the site. Comments: Follow-up inspection conducted to assess overall site conditions on and off the pad. I was accompanied by Sasha Minium, DEP WQS Supervisor for this inspection. Heavy rain within the hours preceding this inspection caused there to be a large amount of water sitting on the pad surface, flowing from the PVC pipe to the west of the pad, and in the wetland and Salt Spring Run to the west of the pad. The 2H and 4H wells are still in flowback. Conductivity readings near the MASS were below 0.8 mS/cm. Taylor Parsons of Falcon accompanied us while we screened the pad surface for conductivity. Conductivities on the pad surface were less than 500 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was on location during the inspection removing water from the pad surface. A work crew was in the process of attaching plumbing from the well heads to the production equipment. A water sample and a conductivity reading was taken from each monitoring point with the exception of SW-6, the wetland near Salt Spring Run, and SW-7, the confluence of the wetland and Salt Spring Run, due to the high volume of water in Salt Spring Run and the wetland and due to the swift current in Salt Spring Run. Outstanding violations.

Violation ID: 842737
Permit API: 059-27350
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Center Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-02-21
Comments: On Tuesday February 19, 2019 I received notification of a produced water release at the Magnum Well Site located in Center Township, Greene County. The release had occurred and was reported to the Department on February 17, 2019. On Tuesday morning I spoke on the telephone with Mr. Corey Giles from EQT Production Company (EQT) regarding details of the incident and the remediation. On February 19 and February 21, I. conducted incident inspections to further assess the situation. The February 21 inspection was conducted after receiving additional requested details from Mr. Giles. On February 17, EQT representatives discovered the release which resulted from a dump valve wash-out. It was estimated that approximately 25-30 gallons was released from the unit as a result of the wash-out. This occurred on the "B" side of the unit and impacted the well pad in front, along side and behind the unit. EQT's remediation contractor, SPSI, excavated the impacted materials for off-site disposal and backfilled the excavated areas. The excavation in front of the GPU was approximately five (5) feet by 24 feet and was approximately six (6) inches in depth at the deepest point. The excavation on the side was approximately five (5) feet by 12 feet and was also six (6) inches and less in depth. The excavation behind the units was approximately five (5) feet by 100 feet and ranged in depth between six (6) inches and 18 inches due to some softer spots that were encountered. Given the excavation dimensions, it appears that no native materials were impacted. As of October 2016, all production equipment is required to be within secondary containment in accordance with 25 Pa. Code, Section 78a.64a(b). These GPUs were not utilizing secondary containment. Due to a recent agreement to obtain compliance with 78a.64a(b) between the Department and EQT, the site is currently In Compliance with Policy (ICP) relative to secondary containment use with production equipment. The release of produced water and impact to the well pad surface is a violation of 25 Pa. Code, Sections 78a.54 and 78a.57a, as well as 35 P.S. Section 6018.301. The operator should respond in accordance with the directions provided in this notice.

Comments: This well was inspected as part of an on going stray gas migration case involving gas migrating into a private water supply (CTS#373559). The well head and casing strings were observed at the time of inspection for leaks, deterioration, and possible failures. As part of the investigation 3 slam bar holes were placed into the ground approximately 1-2 feet from the well head to identify if any methane was migrating from the well-bore. All valves were open and the well is currently equipped for production. 2 check valves were in place on the production lines and were oriented correctly. The operator had this well improperly labeled with the wrong API# and it was requested that it be corrected to reflect the accurate number. VIOLATION: 78.86 - CASING AND CEMENTING – DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Operator failed to correct defect or failed to submit a plan to correct the defect for approval by the Department within 30 days. VIOLATION:78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected. VIOLATION:78.88(d) - OPERATING WELLS – MECHANICAL INTEGRITY OF OPERATING WELLS - Operator failed to immediately notify the Department and take corrective actions to repair or replace defective equipment or casing for wells exhibiting progressive corrosion, rusting or other signs of equipment deterioration that compromise the integrity of the well. VIOLATION: 78.81(a)1 - CASING AND CEMENTING – GENERAL PROVISIONS - Operator conducted casing and cementing activities that failed to allow for effective control of the well at all times At this time the department is requesting an investigation into the possible source of methane to be conducted by the operator.

Violation ID: 933246
Permit API: 051-23196
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Nicholson Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/13/2021
Comments: Inspection conducted in response to a complaint received by the Department of corroded production tanks and possible leak. Arrived on-site at approx. 1130 to conduct investigation. Well appeared equipped for production. No well label was observed on any of the production equipment on site. Recommend Operator affix permanent well label IAW the regulations. Well posting was present but has the wrong permit number on posting (Photo 3). Recommend Operator re-post with the appropriate and correct information for this well. Background conductance reading was taken in a field west of well pad (Photo 1). Conductance value in this location was 170 micro Siemens. Heavy corrosion was observed on production tanks. Holes have developed along the south and west sides of tank (Photos 2/4/5/8/9/10). A large hole (2'x2') has developed on the west side of tank. Production fluid/brine observed approx. 3" below large hole (Photo 5). Conductance of liquid in tank was 14,500 micro Siemens (Photo 6). Tank was located within earthen berm. Conductance readings were taken along the ground on the south and south-west sides of tank (Photos 4 & 8). Values were 3,740 & 4,510 micro Siemens respectively. These values were well above the background conductance reading and indicate a release of production fluid/brine onto the ground. Request Operator determine and provide quantity of release, the method how the quantity was determined, and the duration of the release. Recommend the Operator immediately remove all production fluid/brine from the production tank for proper disposal. It is also recommended that this production tank be removed and impacted soils beneath/adjacent to tank be delineated and areas impacted remediated. Production tank should be replaced once remediation is completed and confirmed by both the Operator and Department. NOTE: Conductance readings taken along the earthen berm were at background. It does not appear at this time that the release has migrated laterally. Violations are being cited related to the release of fluids to the ground and well label/posting. Pending Operator's response, additional violations may be cited.

Comments: On 09/22/2020 DEP representative John Ciccone completed an ADMIN inspection report regarding Chief's YANAVITCH ALTERNATE WELL PAD. The purpose of this report is to document the correspondence between Kellon Balum (Chief) and myself, and to report sample results of sample ID 9544-029.On 08/26/2020, several puddles on the YANAVITCH pad surface were screened for specific conductivity and had elevated conductivities (3 – 4.5 mS/cm). Details regarding this site visit can be viewed in inspection report # 3072591. I contacted Mr. Balum by phone and requested that the puddles be vacuumed. Chief had the puddles vacuumed and estimated that approximately 4 – 5 gallons of fluid were removed from the pad surface. Attached are photos of the puddles before and after the vacuuming event (Please note: Puddle image numbering in this report reflects the numbering provided in the email correspondence and not necessarily the numbering of the puddles in report # 3072591).On 09/22/2020 sample results for sample ID 9544-029 became available. Significant sample results are as follows:Aluminum at 15.45 mg/LIron at 42.28 mg/LMagnesium at 183.7 mg/LManganese at 1.6 mg/LSpecific Conductivity at 3440 umhos/cmStrontium at .825 mg/LDue to the results of sample ID 9544-029 and the actions Chief took on 08/26/2020 to vacuum up the fluid, the following violations cited as pending against API# 015-22743 are now considered cited and immediately corrected:• 25 Pa. It is recommended that sufficiently sized secondary containment is used in order to minimize any releases to the ground. There is no further action required at this time.

Comments: On 12/03/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident response inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1000 hours, weather was 30F and snowing. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).The recently drilled wells onsite are currently undergoing stimulation activities (photo #2); the well permits and secondary containment inspection logs are availbe for review in the company man's trailer (photos #3 and 4).This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by Greylock personnel on 12/03/2024 at 0115 hours. The report detailed a release of approximately 20 barrels of produced fluids onto the pad-wide secondary containment system; the released fluids accumulated at a low point of the containment system and an approximate 2 barrels of produced fluids escaped from the containment system and onto the pad surface. See CTS #: 385569 for more details.Greylock personnel met with me on site to discuss how the release happened and ongoing remediation efforts. Personnel from Penn E and R were also onsite conducting soil sampling in accordance with an Act 2 remediation plan. By the time I arrived, released fluids were already recovered and contaminated soils were being excavated and removed (photos #5 and 6). Soil screening was being conducted as material was removed to ensure that all contaminated soil is recovered. I also screened soils for electrical conductivity (EC) of the affected area; the area field measured for EC at a range of ~1.40 - >4.00mS/cm (photos #7-9).Fluids on the pad surface drain into an infiltration basin which serves as the site's post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photo #10). Greylock personnel had already screened the water draining into the infiltration basin but requested that I also screen it to confirm their results. Water entering the infiltration basin field measured for EC at ~0.54mS/cm; this field measurement was consistent with Greylock's (photo #11).Hydraulic fracturing activities continue onsite (photo #12). Numerous brine, sand, temporary storage tanks/containers are noted and are held on containment (photos #13-15). The site's chemical storage area is located on containment, tidy, and all containers are labeled (photo #16). Production equipment and produced fluids tanks have been installed onsite and are to be put into use when the completed wells go into production (photo #17).Based on the results of this inspection, the following violations are cited against API #: 105-21962:- 35 P.S. 691.402(b)- 25 PA 78a.57(a)- 35 P.S. 6018.301The DEP recommends that Greylock proceeds with Act 2 remediation regarding the aforementioned release.I departed the site at 1200 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: M4 ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/05/2026
Violation Code: OGA3259(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Drilling, altering or operating a well without a permit. Failure to comply with rules or regulations adopted under the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, DEP order, or a term or condition of the well permit.
Violation ID: 8277374
Permit API: 051-24464
Unconventional: Yes
County: Fayette
Municipality: Springfield Township
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 6/05/2026
Comments: An Administrative inspection is being conducted to document a phone conversation that occurred between M4 Energy representative Brad Daugherty and the Department, on 6/05/2026. Daugherty contacted the Department in response to IR 4210309, where the Department noted that "the former well site appears to overall exhibit approximately 50% vegetative growth during this inspection, although some isolated locations on site remain sparsely vegetated". Daugherty objected to the Department's observation, and contended that the vegetation has grown significantly since the Department's 4/17/2026 on-site inspection (IR 4183832). The Department also noted the vegetative growth coverage to be 50% at the time of IR 4183832. The Department explained that although the vegetation on site appeared to have grown taller at the time of IR 4210309, the density of the vegetative coverage appeared to be unchanged and isolated sparse areas were observable on site. The Department then stated the vegetative growth coverage on site will be reevaluated during the next forthcoming follow-up inspection, which is planned for this month. Daugherty requested to meet with the Department on site when this forthcoming follow-up inspection is conducted.The Department then inquired with Daugherty on the purpose of the "feature" shown in Photos 13-15 of IR 4210309. Daugherty explained that the aforementioned "feature" was contoured to restore stormwater flow to pre-existing directions. This is reportedly because a road existed in the former well pad location prior to construction, which reportedly influenced the direction of stormwater flow on site. Further review regarding this "feature" will be conducted by the Department.The violation issued in IR 4095466 shall remain outstanding, as the operator remained out of compliance with the 12/16/2021 COA at the time of IR 4210309.
